result.planSummary: TDD-lite walk extension. Red: wrote test/work-queue.test.ts (11 tests: TC-2.6/2.7/2.9, TC-3.3/3.6 work halves, TC-3.8 work count, TC-5.4 no-work-item clause, restart-survival incl. work items, complete-surface rollback, two CLI in-process legs) plus a process-suite leg, recorded both in the red manifest, confirmed 11 assertion-level failures with red-verify clean. Green: added thread-schema migration v4 (work_item table, committing with the batch); implemented the domain-blind work-queue util (recordItem with deterministic w-<sourceId>-<kind> ids, listItems ordered by queue order, filtered by owner); messages.queueMessageWork with the exact kind gate (user_prompt→prompt_smoothing, tool_result→tool_result_summary, nothing else) and real listQueuedWork; turn-close queueing added to both Story 4 close paths via a closeTurnAndQueueWork helper inside applyEvent, TurnTransitionOutcome extended with queuedWork, real turns.listQueuedWork; pipeline collects items in walk order and surfaces identity-only {workItemId, owner, kind, sourceRef} entries in BatchResult.queuedWork. CLI commands were already routed and went live with the domain implementations. Performed the named exit step: field-by-field review of the shipped WorkItemRecord against the epic's Work Item contract table (lines 348-355 of 01-epic.md) — workItemId unique per thread (PRIMARY KEY), owner values, the three kinds paired to correct owners, sourceRef {messageId}|{turnId}, status literal 'queued', queuedAt from the injected clock, and the batch-result entry shape per line 332 — no drift found.
